entries.german:
Karl IV. genehmigt den eingerückten Brief der Äbtissin und des Konvents des Klosters Pergen in Eichstädter Diözese von Pergen 1359 Sept. 25, womit ihm dieses Kloster Besitzungen zu Hoenstein und Hersbruck für sein Königreich Böhmen verkaufte.

Zeugen: venerabiles Gerlacus Moguntinensis archiepiscopus, per Germaniam, et Guilhelmus Coloniensis archiepiscopus, per Italiam sacri imperri archicancellarii, et illustres Rupertus senior comes palatinus Reni et dux Bavarie, archidapifer, et Rudolfus dux Saxonie, archimarescallus sacri imperii, et venerabiles Johannes Olomuczensis, Johannes Luthomuschlensis, sacre imperialis aule cancellarius, Albertus Swerinensis, Gerhardus Spirensis et Theodricus Wormaciensis ecclesiarum episcopi, illustres Rupertus iunior dux Bavarie, Johannes Opavie et Przymyslaus Teschinensis duces, spectabiles Burchardus burgravius Magdeburgensis, magister curie nostre, Burchardus de Recz et Walramus de Spanheim comites ac nobiles Cuno de Falkenstein, Johannes de Rosemberg, Ulricus de Usk et Thymo de Koldicz, magister imperialis nostre camere, et alii quamplures nostri et imperii sacri principes, nobiles et fideles
entries.english:
Karl IV approves the inserted letter of the abbess and convent of Pergen Abbey in the Diocese of Eichstätt, dated at Pergen on 25 September 1359, by which the abbey sold him estates at Hoenstein and Hersbruck for his Kingdom of Bohemia.

Witnesses: the venerable Gerlacus, Archbishop of Mainz for Germany, and Guilhelmus, Archbishop of Cologne for Italy, archchancellors of the Holy Roman Empire; the illustrious Rupertus senior, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, archsteward, and Rudolfus, Duke of Saxony, archmarshal of the Holy Empire; and the venerable Johannes Olomuczensis, Johannes Luthomuschlensis, chancellor of the Holy Imperial Court, Albertus Swerinensis, Gerhardus Spirensis, and Theodricus Wormaciensis, bishops; the illustrious Rupertus iunior, Duke of Bavaria, Johannes of Opava, and Przymyslaus of Teschen, dukes; the distinguished Burchardus, Burgrave of Magdeburg and our court steward, Burchardus de Recz and Walramus de Spanheim, counts; and the nobles Kuno von Falkenstein, Hans von Rosenberg, Ulricus de Usk, and Thymo de Koldicz, master of our imperial chamber; and many other princes, nobles, and faithful men of ours and of the Holy Empire.
